title: Hawaiian Pizza
subtitle: Ham, pineapple, sweet-savory
description: Ham, pineapple, sweet-savory. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Drain pineapple hard
steps.instruction: Spread pineapple on paper towels and press dry — wet pineapple is the number one cause of soggy Hawaiian centers. Toss ham with a pinch of oregano if you like.

steps.title: Preheat stone to 500°F
steps.instruction: Heat stone or steel at 500°F at least 40 minutes. Shred mozzarella and slice red onion while the oven saturates.

steps.title: Stretch, sauce, and first cheese
steps.instruction: Stretch four 12–14 inch rounds. Sauce lightly; Hawaiian needs less sauce than supreme because pineapple releases juice. Layer half the mozzarella.

steps.title: Ham, pineapple, onion, more cheese
steps.instruction: Distribute ham, pineapple, and red onion evenly — clumps mean some slices are all fruit. Top with remaining mozzarella. Optional red pepper flakes for crews who like heat with sweet.

steps.title: Bake until edges spot brown
steps.instruction: Bake 10–13 minutes until cheese browns and pineapple edges caramelize slightly. Rotate once. If liquid pools in the center, your pineapple was still too wet.

steps.title: Rest and cut for the hall
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes, cut 8 slices per pie. Hawaiian Pizza divides rooms — serve with confidence and a backup pie at 200°F for the converts.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up Hawaiian Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Ham, pineapple, sweet-savory. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
